topics.name: Tense and aspect (progressive, perfect, perfect progressive)
Word forms: noun, verb, adjective, adverb

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct verb form.
options: Rohan are waiting for the right wind.
Rohan is wait for the right wind.
Rohan is waiting for the right wind.
questions.rule: Present progressive = is/am/are + verb-ing. Rohan is singular: is waiting.

options: Our family celebrates Diwali with great joy.
Our family celebration Diwali with great joy.
Our family celebrity Diwali with great joy.
questions.rule: The sentence needs a verb: celebrates. Celebration and celebrity are nouns.

chat: What are you doing on the terrace?
options: I flying my new kite, Papa.
I am flying my new kite, Papa.
I am fly my new kite, Papa.

options: The kites is made by skilled craftsmen.
The kites are made by skilled craftsmen.
The kites were made by skilled craftsmen.
questions.rule: Simple present active make becomes are made; keep the same tense.

questions.source: The wind was too weak to lift the kite.
options: The wind was so weak that it could lift the kite.
The wind was so weak that it could not lifted the kite.
The wind was so weak that it could not lift the kite.
questions.rule: too ... to has a negative meaning, so use so ... that ... could not + base verb.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: We are flying kites since morning.
We have been flying kites since morning.
We have been fly kites since morning.
questions.rule: An action that started in the past and is still going on: have been + verb-ing with since.

options: The thread is too sharp to touch it.

chat: Why didn't you buy the eagle kite?

It was too costly for me to buy.
questions.rule: Use too + adjective + for me + to + verb. too does not go with that.

chat: How do people in Gujarat celebrate Uttarayan?

questions.prompt: Make a sentence in the future perfect.
questions.rule: Future perfect = will have + past participle: will have ended.

chat: Did you enjoy the kite bazar last night?
options: Yes! It was so much fun that we stayed till midnight.
Yes! It was too much fun that we stayed till midnight.
Yes! It is so much fun that we stay till midnight.
questions.rule: last night needs the past (was, stayed), and that goes with so.

chat: Who organises the International Kite Festival?
options: It organised by the State Tourism Corporation.
It is organised by the State Tourism Corporation.
It is organise by the State Tourism Corporation.
questions.rule: Present passive = is + past participle: is organised.

questions.source: The kite was so high that we could not see its colours.
options: The kite was too high that we could not see its colours.
The kite was too high for us to see its colours.
The kite was too high for us not to see its colours.
questions.rule: too ... to already means 'not', so drop not: too high for us to see.

chat: Have the prizes been given out yet?
options: Not yet. They will given at six.
Not yet. They will be given at six.

questions.source: The craftsmen are preparing the special thread.
options: The special thread is been prepared by the craftsmen.
The special thread are being prepared by the craftsmen.
The special thread is being prepared by the craftsmen.

questions.source: The prize was won by a team from Japan.
options: A team from Japan won the prize.
A team from Japan wins the prize.
A team from Japan was won the prize.
questions.rule: Keep the tense: passive was won becomes active simple past won.

questions.source: The bazar is too crowded for us to walk freely.

The bazar is so crowded that we cannot walk freely.
